Boundaries: /auth/prelogin, /auth/key-backup, /auth/recovery-key, /auth/login-key, /auth/encrypted-private-key, /auth/public-key, IndexedDB via keyManagementService.

instruments.evidence: Paths and field names match the K4a routes and structs: login_key, kdf_salt, kdf_iterations, encrypted_private_key, recovery_wrapped_private_key, password, current_password. HKDF labels come from the committed K3 vectors.

PreLoginResponse and KeyBackup mirror the Go JSON tags (omitempty fields optional). RecoveryKeyRequest has json:"password,omitempty" and json:"login_key,omitempty", so the AccountProof spread lands on real fields.
Key derivation has one client implementation (K3), checked against the Node vectors; this phase adds no second one.
Axios serialises the plain objects; no hand-written encoder. The spread proof is asserted present or absent per flow.
Old-scheme fixtures are made by the real encryptPrivateKeyWithPassword, and wrapped copies by the real wrapSecret, not by hand.
Scheme 1 answer and a full scheme 2 answer both sign in.

Hostile pre-login answers: {scheme:2} without salt or rounds made signInSecret return the password (finding k4b-scheme2-without-settings-sends-password). A wrong password, a wrong phrase and a copy under another wrap key are refused.
Empty backup, null old copy, missing recovery copy each tested; the phrase length is K3's rule.
Sibling uploads prove the account: the encrypted-copy upload now carries login_key like the recovery copy.
Every branch reached by a test: scheme 1, scheme 2, malformed answer, unlocked, needs-recovery (missing and wrong), moved, no-exportable-key, recovery ok and refused.
Failures throw to the caller (AuthContext in K4c); unlockAfterSignIn maps an unwrap failure to needs-recovery on purpose, and makes no keys.
KDF settings built in prepareSignUp and moveAccount from the same two K3 constants; the proof shape is one type, AccountProof.

Shape 'secret sent on a fallback path': grepped password in the service; only scheme 1 returns it. Shape 'publish before the private key is held': only createAccountKeys uploads a public key in this phase; AuthContext's old path is replaced in K4c.

instruments.why: No goroutine; JS awaits run in order.

instruments.evidence: Half-way failure: createAccountKeys uploaded the public key first and saved the device key last, and moveAccount moved the account before its phrase copy existed (finding k4b-partial-failure-orphans-keys).
A failed sign-up leaves only wrapped copies that nobody encrypts to; a failed move leaves the account on scheme 1 with a phrase copy of its own key, and the next attempt replaces it.
Controls built after the fixes; see pass 2.
